laborLawData.law: Employment Act Part 4 - Rest Day and Public Holiday Pay
laborLawData.summary: Under Part 4 of Singapore's Employment Act, employees covered (non-workmen earning ≤S$2,600/month, workmen earning ≤S$4,500/month) must be given 1 rest day per week. Work on a rest day at employer's request is paid at 1 day's salary (≤half normal hours), 2 days' salary (>half normal hours), plus overtime for work beyond normal daily hours. Singapore has 11 gazetted public holidays; work on a public holiday earns an extra day's basic pay or a day off in lieu.

laborLawData.summaryEs: Bajo la Parte 4 de la Ley de Empleo de Singapur, los empleados cubiertos deben tener 1 día de descanso por semana. Trabajar en día de descanso a solicitud del empleador se paga a 1 día de salario (≤mitad de horas), 2 días (>mitad de horas), más horas extra. Los 11 días festivos otorgan pago adicional o día compensatorio.

laborLawData.law: Employment Act Part 4 - Working Hours and Overtime (Section 38)
laborLawData.summary: Under Section 38 of Singapore's Employment Act (Part 4), contractual working hours are capped at 8 hours/day (or 9 hours/day for 5-day workweek) and 44 hours/week. Overtime is paid at 1.5x the hourly basic rate, calculated as (12 × Monthly basic salary) / (52 × 44). Maximum overtime is 72 hours/month. Non-workmen earning ≤S$2,600/month and workmen earning ≤S$4,500/month are eligible for overtime pay.

laborLawData.law: Employment Act - Retrenchment Benefit Guidelines (MOM Tripartite Advisory)
laborLawData.summary: Under Singapore's Employment Act, retrenchment benefits are payable to employees with at least 2 years of continuous service (as required by law). Actual amount is determined by contract or collective agreement; MOM Tripartite Advisory recommends between 2 weeks and 1 month of salary per year of service, with prevailing norm around 1 month per year. Employers with 10+ employees must notify MOM of retrenchments within 5 working days of notifying affected employees.

laborLawData.summaryEs: Bajo la Ley de Empleo de Singapur, los beneficios por reducción de plantilla se pagan a empleados con al menos 2 años de servicio continuo. El monto real lo determina el contrato o convenio colectivo; el Consejo Tripartito recomienda entre 2 semanas y 1 mes de salario por año de servicio.

laborLawData.law: Employment Act - Notice of Termination (Section 10)
laborLawData.summary: Under Section 10 of Singapore's Employment Act, either party (employer or employee) may terminate employment by giving prior notice: 1 day for service <26 weeks; 1 week for 26 weeks-2 years; 2 weeks for 2-5 years; 4 weeks for 5+ years. Notice can be waived by payment of salary in lieu. Notice periods must be equal for both employer and employee. If contract specifies a different notice period, the longer of the two applies.

El aviso puede sustituirse por pago del salario correspondiente.

laborLawData.law: Income Tax Act - Individual Income Tax Progressive Rates
laborLawData.summary: Under Singapore's Income Tax Act, tax residents (Singapore Citizens/PRs, or foreigners staying 183+ days in a calendar year) are taxed at progressive rates for Year of Assessment 2024 onwards: 0% on first S$20,000; 2%-22% on S$20,001-S$320,000; 23% on S$320,001-S$500,000; 24% on S$500,001-S$1,000,000; and 24% top rate on income above S$1,000,000. Employers must submit Form IR8A/IR21 for tax reporting; no monthly withholding is required for local tax residents.

laborLawData.summary: Under Thailand's Social Security Act, both employer and employee must each contribute 5% of the employee's monthly wage to the Social Security Fund, with a wage ceiling of 15,000 THB per month (maximum contribution 750 THB per party per month). The government adds 2.75%. Contributions cover old age pension, sickness, maternity, invalidity, death, child allowance, and unemployment benefits.

laborLawData.summaryEs: Según la Ley de Seguridad Social de Tailandia, tanto el empleador como el empleado deben aportar cada uno el 5% del salario mensual del empleado al Fondo de Seguridad Social, con un tope salarial de 15,000 THB al mes.

Employees do not contribute. The fund covers medical expenses, rehabilitation, wage compensation, and death benefits for work-related injuries or illnesses.

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 - Annual Leave (Section 30)
laborLawData.summary: Under Section 30 of Thailand's Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541, an employee who has worked continuously for one full year is entitled to at least 6 working days of paid annual leave per year. The employer schedules the leave in advance or by mutual agreement. Unused annual leave may be accumulated and carried forward if agreed by both parties.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法》佛历2541年第30条,连续工作满一年的员工每年至少享有6个工作日的带薪年假。雇主提前安排休假或与员工协商决定。
laborLawData.summaryEs: Según la Sección 30 de la Ley de Protección Laboral de Tailandia B.E. 2541, un empleado que haya trabajado un año continuo tiene derecho a al menos 6 días laborables de vacaciones anuales pagadas al año.

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 - Sick Leave (Sections 32 and 57)
laborLawData.summary: Under Sections 32 and 57 of Thailand's Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541, employees are entitled to take sick leave as long as they are genuinely ill, and the employer must pay full wages for sick leave up to 30 working days per year. If sick leave lasts 3 or more consecutive working days, the employer may require a medical certificate.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法》佛历2541年第32条和第57条,员工患病期间有权请病假,雇主须按全薪支付每年最多30个工作日的病假工资。若病假连续达3个工作日或以上,雇主可要求员工提供合格医师开具的病假证明。

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act (No. 7) B.E. 2562 - Maternity Leave
laborLawData.summary: Under the Labour Protection Act (No. 7) B.E. 2562 (2019), pregnant female employees are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave per pregnancy, including antenatal check-up days and holidays falling within the leave period. The employer must pay wages for up to 45 days, and the Social Security Fund pays 50% of wages for another 45 days.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法(第7号)》佛历2562年(2019年),怀孕女员工每次怀孕享有98天产假,包括产前检查日和休假期间的节假日。雇主须支付最多45天工资,社保基金再按工资50%支付另外45天。
laborLawData.summaryEs: Según la Ley de Protección Laboral (N.º 7) B.E. 2562 (2019), las empleadas embarazadas tienen derecho a 98 días de licencia de maternidad por embarazo, incluidos días de revisión prenatal y festivos dentro del período.

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 - Working Hours (Section 23)
laborLawData.summary: Under Section 23 of Thailand's Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541, normal working hours must not exceed 8 hours per day and 48 hours per week for general work (or 7 hours/day and 42 hours/week for hazardous work). Employees must be given a rest break of at least 1 hour after working no more than 5 consecutive hours.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法》佛历2541年第23条,一般工作的正常工时每日不得超过8小时,每周不得超过48小时。员工连续工作不超过5小时后须安排至少1小时休息时间。
laborLawData.summaryEs: Según la Sección 23 de la Ley de Protección Laboral de Tailandia B.E. 2541, la jornada normal no debe exceder 8 horas al día y 48 horas a la semana.

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 - Overtime and Holiday Work Pay (Sections 61-63)
laborLawData.summary: Under Sections 61-63 of Thailand's Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541, employers must pay premium rates: overtime on a normal working day at 1.5x hourly wage; work on a holiday at 1x additional for daily-wage employees or 2x total for monthly-salaried employees; overtime hours on a holiday at 3x hourly wage. Total overtime plus holiday work must not exceed 36 hours per week.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法》佛历2541年第61-63条,雇主对超过正常工时的工作须支付加班费:正常工作日加班按小时工资1.5倍支付;节假日工作,日薪员工额外支付1倍小时工资,月薪员工按2倍支付;节假日加班按小时工资3倍支付。
laborLawData.summaryEs: Según las Secciones 61-63 de la Ley de Protección Laboral de Tailandia B.E. 2541, el empleador debe pagar tarifas premium por trabajo extra: horas extra en día laboral a 1.5x, trabajo en festivo a 1x/2x, horas extra en festivo a 3x.

Overtime on a holiday paid at 3x hourly wage

laborLawData.law: Labour Protection Act (No. 7) B.E. 2562 - Severance Pay (Section 118)
laborLawData.summary: Under Section 118 of Thailand's Labour Protection Act (as amended by Act No. 7 B.E. 2562, 2019), an employee terminated without cause is entitled to statutory severance pay based on continuous service: 30 days after 120 days-1 year; 90 days after 1-3 years; 180 days after 3-6 years; 240 days after 6-10 years; 300 days after 10-20 years; and 400 days' wages after 20 or more years.
laborLawData.summaryZh: 根据泰国《劳动保护法(经佛历2562年第7号修订)》第118条,无过错解雇员工须按连续工龄支付法定遣散费:120天-1年支付30天工资;1-3年支付90天;3-6年支付180天;6-10年支付240天;10-20年支付300天;20年及以上支付400天工资。
laborLawData.summaryEs: Según la Sección 118 de la Ley de Protección Laboral de Tailandia (modificada por la Ley N.º 7 B.E. 2562, 2019), un empleado despedido sin causa tiene derecho a indemnización legal según antigüedad continua: 30 a 400 días según antigüedad.
changes: Severance ranges from 30 days (120 days-1 year) to 400 days (20+ years) of wages
New 400-day bracket added by 2019 amendment for 20+ years of service
Statutory severance does not apply if termination is for statutory cause (Section 119)

laborLawData.summary: Under Section 48 of Thailand's Revenue Code, personal income tax is levied progressively: 0% up to 150,000 THB; 5% on 150,001-300,000; 10% on 300,001-500,000; 15% on 500,001-750,000; 20% on 750,001-1,000,000; 25% on 1,000,001-2,000,000; 30% on 2,000,001-5,000,000; and 35% above 5,000,000 THB per year. Employers must withhold PIT monthly under Section 50.
